title: 5-minute stretches before bed
intro: Light stretching before bed can help your body feel more relaxed after a whole day of sitting or standing. This 5-minute routine can be done right on your mattress or on the floor.
muscles: Lower back, hips, glutes, hamstrings, chest and neck. The main focus is relaxing your body and breathing.
steps: Child's pose: Sit on your heels, bend forward, arms straight in front. Hold 45 seconds while taking deep breaths.
Knees to chest: Lie down, hug both knees to your chest. Hold 45 seconds.
Lying twist: Drop both knees to the left, head looking right. Hold 30 seconds, switch sides.
Figure 4 stretch: Cross your right ankle over your left knee, pull your left thigh to your chest. Hold 30 seconds, switch sides.
Finish by lying on your back, breathe in for 4 seconds, breathe out for 6 seconds, repeat 5 times.
mistakes: Bouncing or forcing the stretch until it hurts. A stretch should only feel like a comfortable pull.
Holding your breath. Slow breathing helps your muscles relax more.
Using your phone while stretching. Put your phone away so your body can truly rest.
easier: Put a pillow under your tummy during child's pose or under your knees during the twist.
harder: Hold each stretch for up to 60 seconds, or add a hamstring stretch with your legs straight up the wall.
dose: 5 minutes every night. Can be done daily.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness or tingling. If back pain continues or spreads to your legs, see a doctor or physiotherapist.

faq.q: Do these stretches help me sleep better?
faq.a: Many people feel more relaxed and find it easier to fall asleep. The effect is different for everyone, but it's a good routine to calm your body.

faq.q: Can I do this on the mattress?
faq.a: Yes, especially the lying stretches. For child's pose, a very soft mattress may be less comfortable, so you can do it on a padded floor.
Very little. The purpose is recovery and rest, not burning calories. That's still important for staying consistent with exercise.
